reason: The goal calls for fuel and oxygen, and the sugar is a likely fuel for the muscle fibers.
expectation: The sugar will help supply the fibers for cellular work.

alternatives.reason: The two supplies might need to be combined before reaching the fibers.

effect: The sugar is broken down in the cell fluid, producing some ATP and smaller fuel pieces that continue toward a mitochondrion. Oxygen still needs to be supplied.
reaction: The intermediate breakdown makes me curious about the next stage.
reason: The goal calls for oxygen as well as fuel, and the fibers are now processing sugar.
expectation: Oxygen will help the fibers use the processed fuel to support cellular work.

effect: Oxygen completes the supply step, and the ATP cycle shows how fuel energy supports repeated muscle work. The next goal is to collect and transmit the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The link between ATP renewal and pulling is helpful.
reason: The wrapping is pictured fitting around groups of muscle cells, so it should help collect their pulls.
expectation: The wrapping will gather the fibers into a muscle group.

effect: The wrapping gathers individual cell pulls into larger pulls along the muscle bundles; tendons still need to be attached.
reaction: The arrows make the wrapping's role clear.
reason: The front tendons should transmit the bundled muscle pulls toward their attachment points.
expectation: The front tendons will attach to the bundles to help transmit their pull.

effect: The front tendons formed bending muscles and will need an attachment to move a joint. The rear tendons remain available for the other muscle group.
reaction: The tendon’s role is clear, though its eventual attachment remains open.
reason: The rear tendons appear to be the remaining pieces needed to form the second muscle group.
expectation: The rear tendons will attach to the bundles to form the other muscle group.

effect: The rear tendons formed the straightening muscles, completing the goal of collecting and transmitting the fibers’ pulls. Both muscle groups still need attachments to move a joint.
reaction: The second tendon step was predictable, and I am curious how the two groups will work around a joint.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was most worthwhile: the ATP cycle connected fuel and oxygen to the repeated work of muscle fibers.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the rear tendons felt somewhat repetitive after adding the front tendons, although it completed the second muscle group.

surprise.text: I did not expect sugar breakdown in the cell fluid to produce some ATP before the smaller fuel pieces reached a mitochondrion.

arbitrary.text: The front and rear tendons were clearly associated with separate muscle groups, but the pictures alone did not explain why the front group bends and the rear group straightens; the bones were still absent.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the muscle groups attach to bones and move a joint. The progression from cellular energy to a larger movement is interesting.
